exEn: What a big dog!
note: 'Grosso' = bulky/thick; 'grande' = big/tall/great. Also 'a big problem': un grosso problema.

exEn: The triangle has three sides.
Draw a line.
note: Also a bus/metro line (la linea 1) and a phone line.

exEn: I wear a medium size.
note: 'Il dito medio' = the middle finger; 'la scuola media' = middle school.

exEn: The sky is light blue.
note: Lighter than 'azzurro'.

exEn: They have a huge house.
The door is a rectangle.
Today is a lovely day.
note: 'Giorno' counts days; 'giornata' describes how the day goes: buona giornata!

exEn: We're spending a nice evening together.
note: Like 'giornata' vs 'giorno': 'buona serata!' = have a nice evening.

exEn: I put the letter in the envelope.
note: In shops 'una busta' is often a plastic bag.

exEn: The biscuits are in the box.
Would you like a bag? No, thanks.
A bottle of water, please.

ex: Ti mando una cartolina da Roma.
exEn: I'll send you a postcard from Rome.
There's mail for you.
note: 'Andare alla posta' = to go to the post office. 'Posta elettronica' = e-mail.

exEn: Tonight I'm staying at home.
note: No article: a casa, not 'alla casa'. 'A casa mia' = at my place.

exEn: I go to bed at eleven.
note: No article: andare a letto, essere a letto.

exEn: I eat quickly and go.
note: 'Avere fretta' = to be in a hurry.

ex: La torre di Pisa è famosa.
exEn: The tower of Pisa is famous.
We're visiting the castle.
Is this seat free?
note: 'Un bel posto' = a nice place; 'a posto' = fine, in order.

en: on the right; to the right
exEn: The bank is on the right.
note: 'Girare a destra' = to turn right; 'a destra di' = to the right of.

en: on the left; to the left
exEn: Turn left at the traffic lights.

ex: Vai sempre dritto, poi a destra.
exEn: Go straight on, then right.
note: Also 'sempre diritto'.

ex: La gelateria è aperta anche d'inverno.
exEn: The ice-cream shop is open in winter too.
Tonight we're eating at the pizzeria.
note: 'In pizzeria' without article.

exEn: I live in the city centre.
note: No article: andare in centro.

exEn: Is there a pharmacy near here?
I go to work by motorbike.
note: Short for 'motocicletta'; feminine and invariable: la moto, le moto.

exEn: We're going for a boat ride.
note: Plural with h: barche. 'Barca a vela' = sailing boat.

exEn: Excuse me, a quick question: where is the station?
note: Countable in Italian: 'un'informazione', 'delle informazioni'. 'Ufficio informazioni' = information desk.

ex: Vorrei una camera doppia per due notti.
exEn: I'd like a double room for two nights.
note: 'Camera matrimoniale' = room with a double bed.

exEn: Do you have a single room?
I take the number nine tram.
note: Invariable: i tram.

exEn: On the beach there's a parasol.
note: Bigger than an 'ombrello' (umbrella).

exEn: I go to school on foot.
note: Note 'a piedi' but 'in macchina', 'in treno', 'in bici'.

ex: Andiamo in macchina o in treno?
exEn: Shall we go by car or by train?
note: Means of transport take 'in' without article: in macchina, in autobus, in aereo.

exEn: I'm going to Rome by train.
My brother is very tall.
note: 'Ad alta voce' = aloud. Opposite: basso.

exEn: The table is too low.
note: For a short person use 'basso', not 'corto'. 'A bassa voce' = quietly.

exEn: The cat is thin.
note: Opposite: grasso. 'Latte magro' = skimmed milk.

exEn: It's a modern building.
Today is a special day.
The book is interesting.
Rome is a famous city.
note: 'Famoso per' = famous for.

exEn: It's the last day of school.
note: 'All'ultimo momento' = at the last minute. 'Scorso' = last (in time): la settimana scorsa.

exEn: Is it possible to book?
note: 'Il più presto possibile' = as soon as possible.

exEn: I speak a little Italian.
note: Short for 'un poco'; written with an apostrophe. 'Un po' di' + noun = a bit of.

exEn: Shall we go to the cinema together?
note: 'Insieme a' = together with.

exEn: Perfect, see you at eight!
note: Very common as a one-word reply meaning 'great, that works'.

exEn: This coffee is excellent.
note: Superlative of 'buono' (= buonissimo). 'Ottimo!' = great!

exEn: I'm very well, thanks.
note: Superlative of 'bene'. Opposite: malissimo.

en: alone; by oneself; on one's own
exEn: I live alone.
note: Agrees with the subject: da sola, da soli, da sole.

exEn: Tomorrow I'll definitely come.

ex: Il mio colore preferito è il blu.
exEn: My favourite colour is blue.

ex: La camera da letto è piccola.
exEn: The bedroom is small.
note: Often just 'camera'.

exEn: The keys are in the hall.
note: 'Ingresso libero' = free admission.

exEn: The car is in the garage.
note: Pronounced the French way; invariable.

ex: Il tetto della casa è rosso.
exEn: The roof of the house is red.
There's a picture on the wall.
note: Plural 'i muri' (walls of a house); 'le mura' = city walls. 'Parete' = inside wall.

exEn: Let's take the lift.
The computer is on the desk.
note: A school desk is 'banco'.

exEn: Grandpa is sleeping in the armchair.
Turn on the light, please.
note: 'Accendere / spegnere la luce' = to switch the light on / off.

exEn: The milk is in the fridge.
note: Short for 'frigorifero'; invariable in everyday use.

exEn: The living room is big.
note: 'Sala da pranzo' = dining room; 'sala d'attesa' = waiting room.

exEn: I put the tablecloth on the table.
note: Not to be confused with 'tovagliolo' (napkin).

exEn: I'm heating the pasta in the microwave.
note: Short for 'forno a microonde'; invariable.

exEn: Happy birthday, Anna!
note: Also 'tanti auguri!'

exEn: Have a good trip and see you soon!

en: have a good holiday; happy holidays
exEn: Happy holidays, everyone!

ex: Buon Natale e felice anno nuovo!
exEn: Merry Christmas and happy New Year!
Happy New Year, everyone!
note: Said at New Year; also 'felice anno nuovo'.

exEn: Thanks, have a nice evening!
note: Said when leaving in the evening; 'buonasera' is the greeting on arrival.

exEn: Happy birthday, Grandma!
note: Used for birthdays, name days, Christmas and other occasions.

exEn: See you tomorrow!
note: Literally 'we see each other'. 'Ci sentiamo' = talk soon (by phone).

ex: Vado a fare la spesa, a dopo!
exEn: I'm going shopping, see you later!
note: Also 'a più tardi'.

en: how's it going?; how are things?
exEn: Hi, how's it going? Fine, thanks.
note: Works for both 'tu' and 'Lei'. Answers: bene, tutto bene, così così, non c'è male.

exEn: OK, fine.
note: Very common in speech; also written 'okay'. 'Va bene' and 'd'accordo' are the Italian equivalents.

en: what's your name? (formal); what is it called?
exEn: Excuse me, what is your name?
note: Informal: 'come ti chiami?'. Answer: 'mi chiamo...'

exEn: Nice to meet you, Marco!
note: Formal: 'piacere di conoscerla'. Often just 'piacere!'

exEn: Excuse me, where is the station?
note: Slightly more polite than 'scusi'. Informal: 'scusami'.

exEn: What shoe size do you wear?
note: Shoe size = numero; clothing size = taglia.

exEn: I'm twenty-one years old.
note: 'Venti' drops its final vowel before 'uno' and 'otto': ventuno, ventotto (same for trenta, quaranta...).

exEn: My sister is twenty-three.
note: Written with an accent on the final 'é' (also trentatré, quarantatré...).

exEn: February has twenty-eight days.
note: Venti + otto = ventotto (the 'i' is dropped).

exEn: The train costs two hundred euros.
note: Hundreds are written as one word: duecento, trecento, cinquecento.

exEn: I was born in 2000.
note: 'Mille' becomes '-mila' in the plural: duemila, tremila, diecimila.

ex: Roma ha quasi tre milioni di abitanti.
exEn: Rome has almost three million inhabitants.
note: A noun: 'un milione di' + noun.

exEn: I'd like half a kilo of bread.
note: 'Mezz'ora' = half an hour; 'le due e mezza' = half past two. As a noun 'il mezzo' = means (mezzo di trasporto).

ex: Un chilo di mele, per favore.
exEn: A kilo of apples, please.
note: Short for 'chilogrammo'. 'Un etto' = 100 grams.

exEn: I'm buying a litre of milk.

ex: Il tavolo è lungo due metri.
exEn: The table is two metres long.
note: 'La metro' (feminine) = short for 'metropolitana'.

ex: La stazione è a due chilometri.
exEn: The station is two kilometres away.
note: Abbreviation: km.
